YOAV I. HENIS - CURRICULUM VITAE

Bom: Feb. 20, 1950, Tel Aviv, Israel.
Marital Status: Married to Haya Henis, Feb. 24, 1972.
Daughter, Sivan, born Oct. 13, 1972.
Son, Barak Zeev, born March 25, 1978.

ACADEMIC BACKGROUND

1968 Graduated from high school, Rehovot, Israel.

1968-1971 Military service in the Israel Defence Forces. Released as a Lieutenant.
1971-1974 B.Sc. (Chemistry and Biochemistry), Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem, Israel. Degree awarded CUM LAUDE.

1974-1978 Graduate studies for a Ph.D. degree at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. Degree awarded SUMA CUM IAUDE. Title of thesis: "The Mechanism of the Allosteric and Cooperative Interactions in Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate Dehydrogenase". Thesis carried out under the supervision of Professor Alexander Levitzki at the Department of Biological Chemistry, The Institute of Life Sciences.
1978-1981 Postdoctoral training in cell membrane research employing biophysical methods (fluorescence photobleaching recovery and video image-intensification microscopy) with Professor Elliot L. Elson, Department of Biological Chemistry, Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis, MD.

1981-1985 Lecturer at the Department of Biochemistry, Unit of Neurobiochemistry, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv, Israel.
1985-1988 Senior Lecturer, Department of Biochemistry, Unit of Neurobiochemistry, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv, Israel.

1987/88 Visiting Scientist at the Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research (M.I.T.), Cambridge, MA, at the laboratory of Professor Harvey F. Lodish. Performed research on the biophysical properties of human asialoglycoprotein receptors expressed in the plasma membrane of transfected cells.

1988-present Associate Professor, Department of Biochemistry, Unit of Neurobiochemistry, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv, Israel.

ACADEMIC POSITIONS

1974-1978 Research and teaching assistant at the Department of Biological Chemistry, Institute of Life Sciences, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem, Israel.
1978-1981 Postdoctoral research associate at the Department of Biological Chemistry, Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis, MO.
